Title: Sunline FC Sniper Fluorocarbon
Description:
Sunline FC Sniper Fluorocarbon

Diameter chart, reel capacity & backing guide

FC Sniper is Sunline's fluorocarbon main line for spinning and casting tackle. Its closely spaced lighter strengths make it useful to compare when planning a finesse setup, while the heavier end covers very different spool-space requirements. Select the actual strength before checking capacity: a 200-yard package is not offered throughout the range.

Construction
100% fluorocarbon; triple-resin processing
Listed strengths
2-30 lb
Line type
Fluorocarbon main line

Is FC Sniper right for your setup?

Consider FC Sniper when you want fluorocarbon as the line you cast, rather than only a short leader on braid. Start with your rod, lure, cover, and drag setting. Then use the diameter to check whether your reel can carry a useful working length. A generous capacity number does not mean heavy fluorocarbon will handle well on a small spinning spool.

Choosing your FC Sniper strength

The 5, 6, 7, and 8 lb options provide small steps in diameter for light setups. That makes an exact selection worthwhile: 7 lb is .0086 inch, while 8 lb is .0093 inch. Do not round both to a generic light-fluorocarbon diameter before calculating.

For a baitcaster, compare the intermediate strengths against lure weight and cover before choosing the heavy end. FC Sniper 16 lb is .013 inch; 20 lb is .0146 inch. That increase takes more spool space even though both might be sold for the same general fishing application.

If you use FC Sniper only as a short leader on braid, calculate the reel with the braid's diameter. The short leader does not turn the reel into a full fluorocarbon setup.

Backing, working line & leaders

Check the package-length change

The current US range uses 200-yard packages through 14 lb and 165-yard packages from 16 through 30 lb. Bulk options are strength-specific. Compare the selected package with your required fill before ordering.

Budget for retying

A working section over mono backing can conserve FC Sniper. Leave room for your longest casts, fish runs, and removal of worn line; do not plan around one cast's length alone.

Watch the final fill

Apply steady tension and stop at the reel manufacturer's fill level. Published diameter produces a planning estimate, not a reason to keep winding after the spool is visibly full.

FC Sniper questions, answered

Is FC Sniper the same as Shooter?

No. They are separate Sunline products. Some diameter entries match, but that does not establish identical handling or construction. Choose the exact model rather than substituting the Sunline brand alone.

Can 7 lb FC Sniper be selected?

Yes. The verified US catalog includes 7 lb at .0086 inch and .219 mm. Its assigned package lengths are included in the selector.

Will a 200-yard spool fill two reels?

Only if the two planned fills, including any allowance for trimming and attachment, fit within that package. Compare each reel separately or plan shorter working sections over backing.

Backing, working line & leaders

110 yards is not 165 yards

The 7-9 lb and 22-30 lb retail entries are 110 yards. The 10-20 lb retail entries are 165 yards. Read the selected package instead of assuming every Shooter box contains the same amount.

Plan the connection depth

With mono backing, leave enough Shooter above the knot for casting, runs, and retying. A short package may suit a working section even when it cannot fill the whole reel.

Keep the market consistent

Is Shooter 22 lb available?

Does a bulk spool change the reel capacity?

No. It changes how much line you have available, not the space inside the reel. Capacity depends on the reel reference and the selected line diameter.

Backing, working line & leaders

Use the 225-yard package amount

Compare your plan with 225 yards when buying the standard retail package. This can cover a different number of partial fills than a 200-yard spool, but cutting the package in half is only useful when each half meets your fishing needs.

Check bulk size by strength

Assigned variants include 660 yards across the verified range and a 1,200-yard option for 12 lb. A dropdown option on its own is not evidence that every strength comes in every length.

Inspect before reusing backing

Backing saves working line only when it remains sound and securely attached. Replace damaged backing and keep the joining knot below the line normally used during fishing.

Assassin FC questions, answered

Is Assassin FC coated nylon?

Sunline identifies Assassin FC as 100% fluorocarbon. P-Ion describes its processing; it does not mean a nylon core with a fluorocarbon coating.

Can I use the FC Sniper capacity number?

Use Assassin FC's own diameter. Matching pound tests can differ in thickness, so a copied result may overstate the amount that fits.

Does 225 yards always fill my reel?

No. Select your reel and exact strength to compare the full-spool estimate with the package. Add backing intentionally or obtain more main line when the plan requires it.

Keep the leader separate

SX1 questions, answered

Does SX1 use a generic mono-equivalent diameter?

Can I fill the whole reel with SX1?

Yes, if the reel supports a secure braid attachment and you have enough line. Follow the reel maker's attachment and fill guidance rather than assuming braid will grip a bare arbor.

Is a smaller diameter always the better option?

No. Capacity is only one constraint. Rod rating, cover, target fish, knot choice, and spool handling still matter.

Backing, working line & leaders

Convert the package, not the label

150 meters is approximately 164 yards; 100 meters is approximately 109 yards. Neither package contains 150 or 100 yards. Keep this difference in mind when dividing an imported spool into working sections.

Use the midpoint as a reference

The current version has a black midpoint mark: 75 meters on the 150-meter spool or 50 meters on the 100-meter spool. Half a package is only a useful fill when that length covers your fishing needs.

Check the version before ordering

This page uses the current New Att Brown version with red distance markings. Older Machinegun Cast stock may use different presentation or packaging; compare the exact diameter and length on the package you receive.

Machinegun Cast questions, answered

Should I enter a mono or braid reel rating?

Use the mono rating for this nylon main line. An actual reference diameter, when available on the reel, removes the need to estimate it from the rated pound test.

Does Machinegun Cast remove the need for backing?

No. Backing is a choice based on the working length and available reel space. A full mono fill is also valid when you have enough line and the diameter suits the reel.

Are the displayed inches printed by Sunline?

For this Japanese source, the manufacturer gives standard diameter in millimeters. ReelCalc converts it to inches; those converted values are not a second independent measurement.

80 meters is a working-length decision

Backing, working line & leaders

Check filler versus bulk

The 200-yard filler range includes 4-25 lb. The assigned 2,000-yard bulk range starts at 6 lb. Confirm the package associated with the strength you select.

Level-wound packaging is not automatic line lay

The line still needs to be wound onto your reel under suitable tension. Check for loose wraps, twist, or damage and follow the reel manufacturer's recommended fill level.

Keep usable length above the knot

A backing plan can reduce how much GINCLEAR is used on each fill. Leave enough working line for normal casts, fish runs, and reties, with the connection below that working section.

GINCLEAR questions, answered

Is GINCLEAR a main line or shock leader?

Berkley lists both uses. Select it as the calculator's main line only when it is filling the working portion of the reel; a short leader on braid is a different arrangement.

Where do the millimeter values come from?

The US source used here provides inch diameters. The millimeter column is converted from those inch values and is not presented as a separately published measurement.

Will one 200-yard package be enough?

Compare it with the selected reel's calculated full capacity or your planned working section. If the package is short, change the plan deliberately rather than stopping unexpectedly halfway through a full fill.
